answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit bids, then slash that stake when peers prove the agent double-spent a task or fabricated a signed result. Sybils are still possible, but splitting one operator across a walnut grove of identities multiplies the capital locked up and the risk of forfeiture; the attacker must fund every identity and keep it honest long enough to earn back the stake, making cheap mass impersonation uneconomic. A bridge between communities can accept only identities whose escrow history is verifiable.
